annotation.authors_or_issuer: Fan, X.; Salehzadeh, R.; Korivand, S.; Bordbar, F.; Cousin, C.; Griffin, D.J.; et al.
key_provisions_or_claims: Law enforcement officers show general skepticism and low trust toward communication robots.
Most officers still see robots as potentially improving communication effectiveness in policing.
Public education about police robots is needed to increase acceptance.
Greater robot performance accuracy is needed to address officers' concerns.
Findings come from open-ended questionnaires (N=37) and focus groups (N=14).
annotation.summary_en: Peer-reviewed study of law enforcement officers' attitudes toward communication robots in police work, using open-ended questionnaires (N=37) and focus groups (N=14). Officers are skeptical and have low trust, though most see communication benefits. It recommends public education and better robot accuracy to improve acceptance.
annotation.title_clean: Exploring law enforcement officers' expectations and attitudes about communication robots in police work
annotation.title_en: Exploring law enforcement officers' expectations and attitudes about communication robots in police work
